note: The run after the swapchain edit, and the swapchain is now created: 'Using FIFO present mode' is followed by 'Creating color buffer' rather than the driver's assertion, so the intersection with supportedUsageFlags is what the valid-usage rule asked for. The stop is one line further in, and it is a driver under-report: vkCreateImage returns VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED (-11) for the engine's colour buffer, whose usage is COLOR_ATTACHMENT | INPUT_ATTACHMENT | SAMPLED | STORAGE on R8G8B8A8_UNORM. ps5vk_format_usage (driver/ps5vk_image.c:693-713) maps every one of those bits except INPUT_ATTACHMENT, and ps5vk_image_supported (:735) refuses any usage bit the mapping lacks - but the specification's Format Feature Dependent Image Usage Flags table (formats-v1.4.354.adoc:4242) requires the INPUT_ATTACHMENT usage for any format carrying COLOR_ATTACHMENT or DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT. This is the only usage gap left: vkQuake writes exactly seven image usage flags and the mapping covers the other six.
must_contain: QUAKE ERROR: vkCreateImage failed with code -11
human_check: This is the last mile of start-up, and the failure is a mandatory capability reported as absent rather than a missing feature. The distinction decides whose fix it is: mapping the bit does not implement input attachments - the descriptor type and subpass reads stay R2 - it stops the driver from refusing an image the specification says it must allow, and from answering the same way through vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties2. The port is not patching around it: dropping the bit from the colour buffer would hide a conformance gap that any application meets, and the port's own OIT dodge is about pipelines and descriptors, not about this image. R5 in docs/PS5_VULKAN_REQUESTS.md carries the fix, the acceptance and the scope note that keeps it separate from R2.
